mechanics.name: Déjà Vu
mechanics.currentEffect: The Auras of the three closest Generators that are grouped together are revealed to you. You repair those Generators 4/5/6% faster.
activation: Ends/deactivates when: Highlighted Generators update as the closest grouped trio changes.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.1.0): Removed tracking of highlighted Generators by Maps.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: It highlights a nearby cluster of three Generators and speeds repairs on them.
duration: Aura highlights and repair bonus are available throughout the Trial.
specialInteractions: Maps no longer track the Generators revealed by this perk.

editorial.summary: Highlights the three closest clustered generators and gives you a repair bonus on those generators.
useCases: Break dangerous generator clusters before they become an endgame 3-gen.
Find objectives quickly on indoor or unfamiliar maps.
Spend less rotation time searching and more time actually repairing.
counters: The repair bonus is modest and only applies to the highlighted generators.
A highlighted generator may be unsafe or temporarily blocked, so blindly following the perk can be inefficient.
Experienced coordinated teams already know generator spawns and can reproduce much of the routing value.
pros: Combines objective information and a permanent repair-speed bonus in one General perk.
Directly teaches good generator macro by pointing at the cluster most worth breaking.
Always available and especially helpful on indoor maps.
cons: Does not help during chase or rescues.
The 6% Tier III repair bonus is useful rather than spectacular.
Its information component becomes less necessary as map knowledge improves.
analysis: Déjà Vu is a deceptively strong macro perk because it solves two problems at once. First, it removes time spent wandering for a generator. Second, it identifies the three generators whose proximity is most dangerous if left until late game. Working that cluster naturally spreads the remaining objectives farther apart.

The 6% Tier III repair bonus is not the main reason it ranks this high, but it is meaningful because it applies to the exact generators the perk is already encouraging you to prioritize. The information and speed components reinforce the same decision instead of pulling your build in two directions.

Like Kindred and Windows, some of Déjà Vu’s strength is learning value. A highly experienced SWF that knows generator spawn logic and communicates rotations gains less from the aura information. A returning or Solo Q player gains much more because the perk removes map-search time and provides a clear objective whenever the match feels directionless.

We rank it this position rather than above the chase and hook-economy perks because generator knowledge can eventually be internalized and the speed bonus is modest. But as a free General perk with no setup, no cooldown, and almost no bad-match scenario, it is one of the safest high-value slots in the game.
editorial.verdict: An outstanding default perk, especially in Solo Q or while relearning maps. It is reliable and quietly prevents some of the worst generator layouts Survivors create for themselves.
